compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The BPMN visual workflow editor (ADR 0071, still Proposed, none of its follow-on stories shipped) ships a 2.1 MB tracked JavaScript bundle inside the Python package, keeps 175 MB of untracked `node_modules` in the package tree, and requires a Node 22 CI tier, a `make e2e-deps` target, and an e2e test suite. The only workflow file ever saved with it is an untracked demo from the day it landed. The operator approved removal on 2026-09-06 on the condition that the removal commit is recorded on the visual-eval idea epic `yip-gem-teak` (7013-447f-3084-4241) so the editor can be restored if that idea is revisited. The workflow engine, client-authored workflows, and every other `rebar workflow` subcommand stay.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar workflow edit` no longer exists, no editor module is importable, and the built wheel contains no editor assets; Node and npm are not needed to build, test, or develop rebar. Checked by the CLI, import, wheel, and CI-log assertions in the removal story.
- [ ] The two helpers the prompt library imported from the editor package keep their behaviour in their new home. Checked by the prompt-library write tests.
- [ ] The restore recipe (commit SHA, deleted paths, checkout command) is recorded as a comment on `yip-gem-teak`, ADR 0071 is marked superseded with that SHA, and every doc, changelog, and release-notes surface describes the shipped state. Checked by `rebar show yip-gem-teak` and the docs story's grep assertions.

## Child decomposition
- Removal story: delivers criteria 1 and 2 (Python, CLI, JS bundle, Node toolchain, CI, tests).
- Documentation story: delivers criterion 3 (docs, ADR 0071, changelog, release notes, the restore comment), depends on the removal story for its SHA.
compiled_state.title: Remove the BPMN visual workflow editor, its JS bundle, and the Node CI tier (ADR 0071 never implemented)
